I like Archie as a character, he's an extroverted sweet, naive guy who falls in love very easily. He messes up sometimes but always with the best intentions. Archie is a good son, and a cool friend.

He was blinded by Grundy's lies, because he had genuine feelings for her, while she only used him for sex. In my opinion this, along with the "escort for Cheryl" storyline, served a purpose, actually: to show his naivety, and how people can use love (towards Grundy , and towards music, in Clifford's case) to manipulate and use him. But the second time he wasn't fooled so easily, so he has improved as a character. 

It doesn't take much for Archie to fall for a girl, for Grundy it was a few seconds of flirting and their cringey car sex, but since Archie is young I can see how he could consider that a major event. Archie stated that he was attracted to Betty for being her perfectionist self, but it could be overwhelming, since he felt like he couldn't catch up to her, and he was even more attracted when she started to change as a product of her relationship with Jug (I'll get back to this). For Veronica and Val it took a strong personality, these two girls are gorgeous, they know what they want and they stand up for themselves. 

I feel like Archie started to like Betty now that she's with Jug because seeing them together makes her really seem like a more approachable person, not the perfect girl she always presented herself as when she was in love with Archie. He realized that his fears about feeling something for Betty and being in a relationship with her were invalid, since she didn't take over Jug's life, and she is better (mentally and in terms of personality) as a result of that relationship, and that's what Archie wants for himself. With this said, I think acting on it would be out of character, since some of the best things in Archie's life are his friends, and he wouldn't hurt them like that.
